key_insight: SMI turns each medical concept into an ontology path and combines embeddings across hierarchy levels, making rare and fine-grained codes more meaningful than flat language-model representations.
clinical_relevance: This could improve downstream clinical AI tasks such as mortality, readmission, drug recommendation, and rare drug prediction by preserving clinical hierarchy in concept representations.
method: Defines a Semantic ID as the coarse-to-fine path in an expert medical ontology for each diagnosis, procedure, or medication.
Aggregates frozen biomedical LM embeddings across ontology levels to create hierarchy-aware concept vectors.
Includes a base uniform aggregation and a level-weighted variant tuned on validation data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements on MIMIC-IV across mortality, readmission, drug recommendation, and rare drug prediction, plus more robust patient representations on eICU under cross-hospital shift.
watch_item: Because SMI depends on expert-defined ontologies and validation-based weighting, performance may vary when ontology coverage is incomplete or when moved to new coding systems.
paper_title: SMI: Ontology-Grounded Semantic IDs for Hierarchy-Aware Medical Concept Representation
